messages:
Alyssa: Quick sync - proposal to shrink nightly perf artifacts so diffs are meaningful and storage is sane. We still need fidelity for kernel-selection and batching regressions but not the full qdrep every time.

Sam: Agreed. Current qdrep sizes are brutal (4-9GB). Diffing those is expensive and noisy.

Jordan: Can we export a compact timeline + top-kernel summary and only keep full traces when the cheap diff flags something?

Alyssa: Exactly. Idea: for every nightly run upload a lightweight bundle: kernel-timeline.csv (timestamped kernel start/end rows), top_kernels.txt (nvprof-style top 20 with counts), batch_size_hist.json, kv_cache_timeseries.tsv (step,hit,miss), sample_seq_len_distribution.json, and a small metadata.yaml with capture inputs. Full qdrep only on-demand.

Priya: We should also capture the kernel selection inputs (model name, pinned quantization, seq_len distribution sample, batch distribution). Small JSON is fine.

Sam: Implementation sketch - run nsys as usual, then postprocess into artifacts. Example commands I tested: 
```
nsys profile --output perf_run --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx \
  --sample=ms --duration=120 ./run_inference.sh
nsys export --report=timeline --output perf_run.timeline.csv perf_run.qdrep
nsys export --report=summary --output perf_run.summary.txt perf_run.qdrep
```
Then a Python extractor parses the timeline and emits kernel-timeline.csv + top_kernels.txt + batch histogram.

Alyssa: For KV cache, exporter should sample the first N tokens (say 200) and write a TSV with columns: wall_time_ms, step, kv_hit, kv_miss. That lets us see cold-start effects.

Jordan: Storage plan: s3://perf-artifacts/lightweight/<run-id>/ retained 30 days. Full traces to s3://perf-artifacts/full/<run-id>/ with 7d retention by default. If the diff step marks a run as regressed, we promote that full artifact to long-term.

perf-bot: nightly-perf completed: run_id=perf-2026-02-04-01, lightweight bundle uploaded to s3://perf-artifacts/lightweight/perf-2026-02-04-01/

Priya: Gating rules proposal: run a cheap diff on the lightweight metrics vs baseline. If p50/p95/p99 latency goes up beyond thresholds (p99 > 5% or p95 > 7%), or any top-5 kernel time increases >8%, open a perf-blocker and fetch full qdrep.

Sam: Also add a PR-level capture: small-duration nsys (30s) on PR runners for changes touching serving/runtime or kernels. If the PR-run shows a suspicious hotspot the extractor attaches the lightweight bundle to the PR for reviewers.

Alyssa: TODOs:
- perf/tools/nsys_extractor.py that takes perf_run.qdrep and emits: kernel-timeline.csv, top_kernels.txt, batch_hist.json, kv_timeseries.tsv, sample_seq_len_distribution.json, metadata.yaml
- GH Actions job `pr-perf-capture` with `if: contains(paths, 'serving/runtime/**') || contains(paths, 'eng-runtime/**')` to run short capture on PRs
- infra lifecycle rule to enforce S3 TTLs and copy promoted full traces to long-term prefix
- dashboard diff formatter changes to visualize kernel name changes and per-kernel latency deltas (highlight new kernels or changed kernel implementations)

Jordan: Important note: kernel-selection decisions depend heavily on seq_len distribution. Please include a small sample (first 100 seq lengths) in the bundle so we can repro selection heuristics.

Sam: I'll prototype the extractor tonight. Plan to use nsys export + a lightweight parser instead of parsing qdrep binary. We can keep the qdrep local until a regression is triggered.

Priya: Security: scrub environment variables, git tokens, and any customer identifiers from exported metadata.yaml before upload. Add a validation step that rejects uploads with "AWS_KEY" or similar present.

Alyssa: Nice. One UX asks: the diff dashboard should link directly to the lightweight bundle and show a quick flamebar for top-10 kernels (server-side SVG). If people need the full flame they can click to fetch full qdrep.

perf-bot: perf-extractor job queued for perf-2026-02-05-primer (triggered by @Sam)

Sam: Also adding an optional reproducibility script `perf/repro/run_with_capture.sh` that takes the metadata.json and replays the input distribution to reproduce the capture locally. Will include in extractor output.

Alyssa: OK let's land extractor + GH action in staging, run at least 5 nights, evaluate false positives/negatives, then promote. thanks!
